why: B is false, as its author predicted, and A ⇒ ¬B is proved (A_to_not_B). B asks for an orientation ô of DET(f̂,(t,x)) with ô(L̂) = conjDet(extDet(ω(L))) for every L ∈ Lin(f,x), i.e. the text's h ↦ h̃ WITHOUT the sign (−1)^{dim coker L} that the project puts into extDetN. Counterexample: the trivial bundle ℝ¹×ℝ¹→ℝ¹, f = 0 (graph section, sc-Fredholm), translation chart at x = 0, t = 0, S = 0. Lin(f,0) contains L₀ = 0 (dim coker 1) and L₁ = id (onto; from s = graph id). Conjugating B's ô back and pulling it back along extDetN (extPullRay, an orientation by A's isLineOrientation_extPull) gives Φ with Φ(L) = (−1)^{dim coker L}·ω(L); Φ = ω at L₁, hence everywhere on the convex Lin(f,0), contradicting Φ(L₀) = −ω(L₀). So A ⇒ B is false (not_A_to_B) and B ⇒ A holds only ex falso. The refutation uses from A only the continuity of extDetN (through the hypothesis); an A-free refutation would have to re-prove that continuity (coord_extDet, the Proposition 6.24 chart coordinates), which was not attempted.
